cards.text: Years ago Jacob ran for his life, because his brother Esau planned to kill him (Genesis 27:41-43). Now Jacob has sent droves of livestock on ahead as a gift for Esau (Genesis 32:13-21). Then Jacob looks up and sees Esau coming toward him with four hundred men. FOUR. HUNDRED.

cards.question: Esau is coming with four hundred men. Jacob divides the ___ among his wives Leah and Rachel and the two maidservants.

cards.text: Next, Jacob lines up his whole family to meet Esau, group by group.

cards.question: Jacob lines up his family to meet Esau, group by group. At the very rear, he puts ___ and her son Joseph.
Esau and his four hundred men are coming, and Jacob's family is lined up. Where does Jacob himself go?

answers.text: Off to the side with his servants

cards.text: Earlier, Jacob asked God to deliver him from his brother Esau (Genesis 32:11). Now he bows to the ground seven times as he approaches his brother.

cards.question: Jacob is bowing low as Esau and his four hundred men get close. Esau runs to Jacob and embraces him.

cards.text: Jacob had the gifts, the lineup and seven bows all worked out. Esau just RUNS to him, throws his arms around his neck and kisses him, and they both weep.

cards.question: Esau looks up, sees the women and children, and asks who they are. How does Jacob describe the children?

answers.text: God graciously gave them to him
God gave them as a reward for his work
God sent them to make peace with Esau

cards.text: Then the family comes forward, group by group. The maidservants and their children, then Leah and hers, then Joseph and Rachel, and every one of them bows down.

cards.question: Esau asks Jacob, "What do you mean by sending this whole company to meet me?" What does Jacob say?

answers.text: To find favor in your sight
To repay the debt I owe you
To show the riches in my hand

cards.question: Jacob offers Esau the droves of livestock as a gift. Esau accepts them as soon as Jacob offers.

cards.text: Esau says he already has plenty and tells his brother to keep what belongs to him. But Jacob insists, "No, please!"
Then Jacob tells Esau, "For indeed, I have seen your face, and it is like seeing the face of God…"

cards.question: Jacob says seeing Esau's face is like seeing the face of God because Esau has received him favorably.

cards.text: Jacob says God has been gracious to him and he has all he needs, and he keeps pressing until Esau accepts. One brother has plenty, the other has all he needs, and it took all THAT just to hand over a gift.
Gift settled. Esau says, "Let us be on our way, and I will go ahead of you."

cards.question: Esau wants them to travel together with him leading the way. What reason does Jacob give for holding back?

answers.text: His children are frail and his herds are nursing
His servants are worn out from the long trip
His wives need to rest for a few days first

cards.text: Jacob says if they're driven hard for even a day, all the animals will die. Same with my dough, friend: rush it and the whole batch comes out flat.

cards.question: Jacob asks Esau to go on ahead and says he'll follow slowly, at a pace the livestock and children can handle, until he comes to him at ___.

cards.text: Esau tries one more thing. He offers to leave some of his people with Jacob.

cards.question: Jacob takes Esau up on his offer to leave some of his people with him.

cards.text: Jacob says, "Why do that? Let me find favor in the sight of my lord." So that day Esau starts on his way back to Seir.

cards.question: Esau heads back to Seir, but Jacob goes on to a different place. What does Jacob build there for himself?

cards.text: Jacob builds a house for himself and shelters for his livestock. I spent years in a junk drawer, so trust me, I respect a man who finally gets his own space.

cards.question: Because of the shelters Jacob builds for his livestock there, the place is called ___.

cards.text: After coming from Paddan-aram, Jacob arrives safely at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan and camps just outside the city. Seven bows and four hundred men later, safely sounds REAL good.

cards.question: Jacob pitches his tent just outside the city of Shechem, on a plot of ground belonging to the sons of Hamor, the father of a man named Shechem. Jacob buys that plot of ground from them.
Jacob pays the sons of Hamor a hundred pieces of silver for his plot. What does he set up on it?

cards.text: He calls the altar El-Elohe-Israel. Stay close, friend, because Jacob's family still has plenty of road ahead of them.
